routes.name: Northeast Ridge
gear: single rack of cams to #2 Camalot
hazards: Variable, sometimes loose rock along the ridge.
Exposed traverse ledges around overhanging sections.
Route-finding required to link the ridge's wandering, traversing line.
routes.overview: The peak's classic technical route: 4 pitches of alpine rock up the northeast ridge, established by the Firey party in 1970, with a steep 5.5 crux about 100 ft below the summit.
routes.beta: The route climbs the ridge in 3-5 pitches (typically done in 4) at 5.5. Rock quality ranges from highly questionable to pretty solid. The line involves a rightward traverse around overhanging walls, narrow exposed grass ledges, and ridge-crest climbing on somewhat loose alpine rock before a steep crux section roughly 100 ft below the summit.
routes.turnaround: Because the descent is by rappel and the multi-day approach/exit is long, start early enough to be off the ridge and back at camp well before dark, and turn around at the first sign of incoming weather given the exposed, traversing nature of the crux.
routes.rappels: About 5 rappels down the ridge, four single-rope and one double-rope, from existing fixed slings; a 70 m rope reaches most stations, and one party managed on a 50 m rope plus a tagline
routes.comms: No reliable cell coverage in the Terror/Crescent Creek basins or on the peak; carry a satellite communicator and know NPS Park Dispatch, (360) 873-4500.
routes.descent: Rappel the route (1-2 ropes; 70m recommended for most stations) back to the base of the ridge.
routes.detailed_rack: A single set of cams to a #2 Camalot, small-to-medium stoppers, and double (shoulder-length) slings are useful given the wandering, traversing nature of the line.
what_to_bring: overnight/bivy gear for the multi-day approach
approach shoes plus rock shoes or sturdy boots for 5.5 rock
pro_tips: A 70m rope reaches most rap stations comfortably; carrying a tagline (as one party did with a 50m) is a lighter alternative.
The route can be linked into as few as 3 pitches by a strong party or broken into 5 for shorter belays through the loose sections.
watch_out: Rock quality varies from loose/questionable to solid — test holds carefully.
Narrow, exposed grass ledges partway up the ridge.
The crux steep 5.5 section is about 100 ft below the summit — stay attentive after already climbing 3+ pitches.
routes.pro_needs: Single set of cams to #2 Camalot size, small-medium stoppers; double slings useful for the traverse and loose terrain.
routes.best_season: Ascents are made from mid-July through early October; the route is a popular add-on for parties in Crescent Creek Basin climbing Terror, Himmelhorn, or the McMillan Spires.
routes.approach: Via the multi-day Goodell Creek approach to a camp on the Chopping Block ridge (~6,400 ft) or the col separating the peak from the main Picket Range; from there, walk and scramble (some exposed 3rd class) southwest to the base of the ridge.
routes.descent_text: Descend by rappelling the ridge itself — most parties use a 70m rope to reach most stations comfortably; one reporting party got down on a 50m rope with a tagline. Existing fixed rap slings have been reported along the route.
routes.bail: Rappel the ridge from any station; fixed anchors of typical Cascades rappel tat have been reported at multiple points.

road.name: Goodell Creek Road (off SR-20) / North Cascades Highway
road.status: Goodell Creek spur road and trailhead are accessible year-round via SR-20 from the west (Sedro-Woolley/Marblemount/Newhalem side)
road.driveNote: From Newhalem on SR-20, turn north onto the unpaved Goodell Creek Road (across the highway from the Goodell Creek/Newhalem group campground) and continue to parking at the end of the road.
road.seasonalGate: The seasonal SR-20 closure gate is well east of here, near Ross Lake/Washington Pass, and does not affect access to Newhalem or the Goodell Creek Trailhead

climate.fall: Possible in early October in a dry year, per documented trip reports, but daylight and weather windows shrink fast.
climate.summer: Best window is Jul-Sep; a handful of parties have climbed it into early October in good conditions.
climate.typical: Cool, wet, marine-influenced North Cascades climate with orographic precipitation off Pacific weather systems.

emergency.notes: Extremely remote cross-country terrain; NPS notes the closest advanced-life-support ambulance comes from Concrete (~1 hour) and reception is unreliable throughout the basins — carry a satellite communicator.
emergency.county: Whatcom/Skagit County line area (trailhead access is via Skagit County; summit is near the Whatcom-Skagit line)
emergency.rangerStation: North Cascades NP Wilderness Information Center, Marblemount, WA: (360) 854-7245
emergency.nearestHospital: Nearest hospital is in Sedro-Woolley, WA, roughly 90 minutes by road from the trailhead (per NPS)

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Late July to mid-September, after the ridge camp and Barrier slabs melt out but while snowmelt still supplies camp water

July.reason: Snowfields linger in Crescent Creek Basin and moats need care early in the month, but water is plentiful and days are long.

June.reason: The Terror Creek climb to the ridge camp and the scramble to the ridge base are still largely snow-covered, with moats forming.

August.reason: Snowfields shrink, the exposed grass ledges and loose ridge rock are dry, and the 3rd-class walk to the base is straightforward.

October.reason: Ascents reach early October, but the first snow coats the grassy traverse ledges and short days crowd a multi-day approach.

September.reason: Stable weather and dry rock; the ridge camp may lose its snowmelt water late in the month, so plan to carry or melt.
